clue.text: An odd escort for an older person

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: odd means strange or irregular, so the letters of the word escort are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A mismatched companion chosen to accompany an elderly person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges ESCORT into CESTOR; the opening 'An' stays as it is in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A forebear from whom one is descended is, by definition, an older person in the family line.

clue.text: Raced over line with not much room to spare

definitions.text: with not much room to spare

indicators.note: over signals that the word before it is turned back to front

parts.note: raced means ran
a row is a line of things side by side

explanation.surface: A runner hurtles across the finishing line, winning by a whisker.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a tight margin or squeeze leaves little room, as in a close escape.

clue.text: Non-striking bonus

definitions.meaning: in cricket, runs such as byes and wides are credited to no batsman's stroke
something additional on top of what is expected

explanation.surface: A reward paid to workers who stayed off the picket line.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the striker is the batsman facing; runs scored other than off the bat are called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean something added beyond the normal: a cricket run not hit, and an additional reward.

clue.text: Mike had to play leading part in operetta

indicators.note: to play with letters is to toy with them and rearrange them, applied to the three words before

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An actor called Mike landed the starring role in a light opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' looks like theatre talk but rearranges MIKE HAD TO. The title role of Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera is the Japanese emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilbert and Sullivan's operetta takes its name from its emperor character, a principal role.

clue.text: A verbal thrust?

parts.note: in fencing a quick return thrust after parrying; by extension a sharp witty retort in words

explanation.surface: A pointed remark that stabs like a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: The fencing term for a counter-thrust is also used for a quick, cutting reply in conversation.

clue.text: Saucy antics?

definitions.meaning: pickled flower buds used in sauces such as tartare

explanation.surface: Cheeky, risqué behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saucy' reads as cheeky but points to the pickled buds that go into sauces.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both frolicsome pranks and the small pickled buds that flavour sauces.

clue.text: One provides seedless apples for cooking

definitions.text: One provides seedless apples for cooking

parts.words: One provides seedless apples for cooking
parts.note: a kitchen tool removes the pips and centre from apples before baking

explanation.surface: A grower who supplies pip-free cooking apples.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a fruit supplier; it is a kitchen gadget that takes the cores out.
explanation.definitionFit: This utensil removes the central pips of apples, leaving them seedless for baking.

clue.text: Perfectly proficient?

parts.note: the proverb says repetition makes perfect, so someone skilled through rehearsal fits

explanation.surface: Someone who is flawlessly skilled.
explanation.walkthrough: Plays on the proverb 'practice makes perfect'.
explanation.definitionFit: Skilled through long repetition and rehearsal; the proverb links rehearsal to perfection.

clue.text: Criminal set?

definitions.meaning: a fence, someone who handles stolen goods
a radio or television apparatus that picks up signals

explanation.surface: A gang of crooks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal set' reads as a gang; it is two separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a handler of stolen goods and a radio or TV apparatus.

clue.text: Squirm and wither, wanting right to advance

indicators.note: to advance is to move forward, so one letter shifts nearer the front of the word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone writhing and shrivelling in discomfort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to advance' moves the R of WITHER forward, after the W.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to twist and wriggle the body, as in pain or embarrassment.

clue.text: Talk of cut after backing strike

indicators.note: after places the word for cut behind the other piece
backing means going in reverse, so the word for strike is read backwards

parts.note: to rap is to strike sharply
to lance is to cut open, as a boil

explanation.surface: Discussion of a pay cut following a reversed strike decision.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a particular way of speaking or idiom, as in 'common usage'.

clue.text: Their job is to certify, not sign

parts.note: taken as written
Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: These officials authenticate documents rather than putting their names to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sign' looks like a verb about signatures; it is a star sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Public officials who witness and attest signatures and documents.

clue.text: Keep thanks in check

indicators.note: in places the word for thanks within the word for check

parts.note: to rein is to check or restrain
ta is informal British for thanks

explanation.surface: Gratitude being held under control.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to continue to possess something rather than give it up.

clue.text: Confidence shared by the whole house

definitions.text: Confidence shared by the whole house

parts.words: Confidence shared by the whole house
parts.note: an actor's aside meant to be heard by the entire theatre audience

explanation.surface: A secret that every member of the household knows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house' suggests a home; it is a theatre audience.
explanation.definitionFit: On stage, a supposedly private aside is spoken loudly enough for the whole auditorium.

clue.text: Unwilling to give credit

parts.note: not inclined to give credence, that is to believe

explanation.surface: A lender refusing to extend a loan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'credit' suggests banking; here it means belief.
explanation.definitionFit: Doubting people do not readily believe claims, withholding credence.

clue.text: WWII fighter that gets the wind up

definitions.meaning: the Hawker fighter plane of the Battle of Britain
a violent tropical storm whips up strong winds

explanation.surface: A wartime pilot who is frightened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets the wind up' is British slang for being scared, but here it is literal storm wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Names both a famous RAF single-seat aircraft and a tropical cyclone of very high winds.

clue.text: Plan to study piece of church architecture

parts.note: to con is an old word for study or learn
a spire is the tapering top of a church tower

explanation.surface: An intention to research a feature of a church building.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to plot together secretly.

clue.text: Got up and blushed pink

parts.note: rose means got up
coloured means went red in the face

explanation.surface: Someone stood and went pink with embarrassment.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: tinted a pale reddish hue.

clue.text: Journeyed round the world?

parts.note: travelled in a circuit around a planet, as a satellite does

explanation.surface: Someone who travelled the globe.
explanation.walkthrough: Suggests a globetrotter; it is a satellite's path.
explanation.definitionFit: Circled a planet in a fixed path, like a satellite or spacecraft.

clue.text: Phone about account that's for betting on?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for phone goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: to ring is to phone

explanation.surface: Ringing a bookie to check an account used for placing bets.
explanation.definitionFit: Horses and dogs competing at the track are what punters wager on.

clue.text: Fly in different directions after trial's overturned

indicators.note: after places the compass points behind the other piece
overturned means flipped over, so the word for trial reads backwards

parts.note: a test is a trial
S and E, south and east, are two different compass points

explanation.surface: A verdict is overturned and people scatter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' turns TEST into TSET. 'Fly' looks like a verb; it is the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: An African insect, a blood-sucking pest that spreads sleeping sickness.

clue.text: Compel payment to be precise

definitions.meaning: to demand and obtain money, as in levying a toll
accurate and correct in every detail

explanation.surface: Forcing someone to pay the correct amount.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for demanding payment and an adjective for being accurate.

clue.text: Blunt criticism of decent chap joining club

parts.note: a brick is old British slang for a reliable, good-hearted person
a bat is a club, as in cricket

explanation.surface: Harsh words directed at a nice man joining a society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' suggests a society; it is a bat.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a piece of brick thrown as a missile; figuratively a harsh remark or insult.

clue.text: Cook steak for a poet

indicators.note: to cook figures is to doctor them, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Preparing a steak dinner for a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: John, the English Romantic who wrote odes to a nightingale and to autumn, is an example.

clue.text: They are empowered to go over our heads

definitions.text: They are empowered to go over our heads

parts.words: They are empowered to go over our heads
parts.note: powered flying machines pass overhead

explanation.surface: Officials authorised to bypass ordinary people's authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go over our heads' suggests bypassing someone; literally, flying above. 'empowered' means engine-powered.
explanation.definitionFit: Planes and helicopters are engine-driven machines that fly overhead.

clue.text: Song about sailor in desert land

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the song goes around the sailor

parts.note: an aria is a song in opera
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A ballad about a mariner lost in the desert.
explanation.definitionFit: The great peninsula of south-west Asia is largely arid sand and rock.

clue.text: For one to laze is unusual

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters of the words before are put in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Idling is uncharacteristic for this person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For one' means one who is for a cause, a fervent supporter.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanatical supporter is cryptically someone very much 'for' a cause.

clue.text: Olympic riding event outfit will get silver with ecstasy

parts.note: a dress is an outfit
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A rider's outfit will win a silver medal in high spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: An equestrian discipline in which horse and rider perform precise schooled movements.
